text:
liam: Heads up — us-west gpu pool hit 98% util at 09:12, queues growing and egress latencies spiking (p50->p95 jump). Noticed a lot of best-effort jobs from free-tier clients saturating warm-pools.
anya: Ugh, saw that. Any network blips or is this pure GPU pressure?
matt: No network errors in logs. It's sustained allocation — many long-context requests and a couple of bulk-embed jobs.
liam: Paste from monitor: `gpu_pool_usw1: util=98.2% queue_len=428 inflight=9600 avg_latency=312ms`
jess: Can we soft-divert non-SLA traffic to eu-central or to the cold spare lane? Trying to avoid mass evictions.
liam: We tried cross-region divert earlier and saw cold-start tail latencies — some spike to 1.2s which broke a couple UX checks. Thinking of a gradual panning strategy instead of abrupt failover.
anya: Define panning?
matt: panning = slowly shifting a fraction of new traffic to other regions/pools (e.g., 5% steps) while keeping hot cache for gold traffic. Less cold-start shock.
liam: Proposal: 1) increase per-tenant admission control for free-tier (token-rate cap) 2) enable panning policy for best-effort lanes 3) evict oldest preemptible warm pods if we still exceed 95% for >5m
jess: Sounds reasonable. For (1) can we do a quick throttle via ingress? Example command: `redwoodctl rate-limit set --tenant free --rps 10 --window 60s`
anya: Also suggest falling back to quantized smaller model for best-effort (model_fallback: r-mid -> r-mini-q4) to reduce GPU time. :thinking_face:
matt: Agree. If we can reduce average tokens per request by 30% that buys headroom. We'll need model compatibility checks in the routing layer.
liam: Quick config I sketched for routing layer (dry-run):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  overflow_mode: pan-and-evict
  pan_step: 0.05   # 5% increments
  pan_interval_secs: 120
  priority_lanes:
    gold: keep
    standard: allow
    best_effort: divert_to: [eu-central-1, us-east-1]
  fallback_model:
    best_effort: r-mini-q4
  preempt_eviction:
    threshold_util: 0.95
    grace_period_secs: 300
```
matt: That `pan_step` approach seems safe. We should add a circuit-breaker: if p95 latency in target region > 800ms for 2m, pause panning.
jess: Who's oncall in us-west right now? @oncall please watch for alerts, I'll prepare the throttle job.
oncall: oncall here — watching. If p95 crosses 1s I'll trigger emergency rollback to strict admission control and priority-only routing.
liam: I'll kick off a low-risk change: set free-tier rps to 8 and enable pan_step dry-run with metric tagging.
anya: Thanks. Can someone post the exact CLI commands once applied? I'll coordinate a post-mortem if this degrades any customer flows.
matt: Applying throttle now: `redwoodctl rate-limit set --tenant free --rps 8 --window 60s --region us-west-1` — done.
liam: Enabled pan dry-run (`--dry-run`) so we can observe diverted fraction without actually routing. Tagging metrics under `routing.pan.dryrun.usw1`.
sre-bot: ALERT suppressed — util 96.7% -> 92.1% after throttle. Queue_len dropped to 210.
jess: Nice, visible improvement. Next step if stable for 3m: flip dry-run -> active for best-effort.
liam: Agreed. I'll wait 3m then roll pan to 15% divert in steps.
anya: Filing a short ops note after this: /ops/notes/usw1-capacity-2001234567.
liam: Thanks team. Follow-up: once stable, let's run a cost analysis on how many requests moved cross-region vs how much CPU/GPU time saved.
jess: Will do. :thumbsup:
